description: The Higgs is a team of 6 members passionate about space, science, technology, and innovation. Inspired by the Higgs boson, we combine skills in engineering, programming, research, design, and problem-solving to create meaningful solutions. We value teamwork, creativity, and learning, and we are excited to take on the NASA Space Apps Challenge.
summary:
UNQUALIFIED is a first-person mission-design simulator built in Unity that runs in any web browser. The player is the leader of 5 engineers in a small space-agency office. The game contains over 16 missions of training targets, such as real asteroids; but the catch is: the team resigns one by one and the player inherits six stations (structure, propulsion, trajectory, telecom, power and thermal, payload), and ends up designing the whole missions alone.
Each mission arrives as a ConOps email with a target, required instruments, a science goal, a budget, a launch window and a NASA risk class (A–D). The player designs the spacecraft and a two-stage rocket with real engines, plans the trajectory and launches. Success is decided by physics, not chance, using the rocket equation, numerical flight integration and 16 failure rules, with a report that explains what failed and why.
Mission design is usually taught as theory. UNQUALIFIED turns real NASA/JPL data (Horizons ephemerides of the 2029 Apophis flyby, Saturn V and SLS engines, the Deep Space Network, NPR 8705.4 risk classes) into decisions with consequences, so players learn systems thinking by doing, failing and fixing.
details:
Players design 16 missions in a 3D office with six engineering stations. For each one they read the ConOps, design every subsystem (a rocket from 13 real engines, trajectory, telecom, power, instruments), launch and get a report. Flight is integrated with Earth, Moon and Sun gravity and drag, using JPL Horizons ephemerides.

Learning by failing: every failure is explained. Reference designs disappear as engineers resign, and manuals with practice questions guide beginners. Free, browser-based, in English and Spanish.

Help students and teachers understand real mission design and inspire aerospace careers, especially in Latin America, around the real 2029 Apophis flyby.

Unity 6 and C# (WebGL), VS Code, Python, the NASA/JPL Horizons API, NASA technical data, the Spaceflight News API, free Unity Asset Store models and ChatGPT for comic art.

The story is the tutorial: each resignation hands you a new subsystem. Papers, Please-style pressure (salary, rent), a retro Windows 95 PC, comics and code-generated chiptune music.

Realism vs. playability (a 2D model so it runs in a browser), honest labels for real vs. simplified data, a gentle learning curve, a campaign validated as winnable, and licensing. The game's mechanics are done by researched and modified theoretical models by our team in order to make the game not only fun, but also relatively reliable aproximation of how a real objects should travel through space, being inspired by the tool "GMAT".
